files.README.md:
# drizzle-postgresql-repository-commits

Data access layer generated by [DB2CRUD](https://github.com/RaulEstevezA/DB2CRUD) for a database that already exists: entities, repositories and services with Drizzle 0.45. It does not create or migrate the database.

## Settings

- Database: postgresql; code: asynchronous (every method returns a Promise).
- Entities: written for the tables the input had no class for.
- Services: take and return the entities.
- Transactions: every repository write is committed at once.
- Lists: lists return pages by offset and limit.

## Layout

```text
src/schema.ts          the Drizzle tables, as the database has them
drizzle.config.ts      where drizzle-kit finds the tables and DATABASE_URL
src/database.ts        the database: DATABASE_URL, through its driver
src/errors.ts          NotFoundError, ConflictError, ValidationFailedError: no HTTP codes
src/unit-of-work.ts    the repositories of every table, and the transaction of each operation
src/entities/          one entity per table
src/repositories/      one repository per table
src/services/          one service per table
test/                  repositories against a database, services on the in-memory repositories
crud-contract.json     what was written, for CRUD2Controller
```

## Running the tests

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck && npm run build
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://app:app@localhost:5432/app npm test   # a real, disposable database: it is emptied
```

/** The repositories of every table, and the transaction of each service operation. Every repository write is committed at once; `transaction()` only groups the code. */
import type { Executor } from './database.js'
import { SqlAuditLogRepository } from './repositories/audit-log.js'
import { SqlCategoryRepository } from './repositories/category.js'
import { SqlCustomerRepository } from './repositories/customer.js'
import { SqlOrderRepository } from './repositories/order.js'
import { SqlOrderLineRepository } from './repositories/order-line.js'
import { SqlProductRepository } from './repositories/product.js'
import { SqlProductTagRepository } from './repositories/product-tag.js'
import { SqlTagRepository } from './repositories/tag.js'

/** What services depend on: a repository per table and a transaction. */
export interface UnitOfWork {
  readonly customers: SqlCustomerRepository
  readonly categories: SqlCategoryRepository
  readonly products: SqlProductRepository
  readonly orders: SqlOrderRepository
  readonly orderLines: SqlOrderLineRepository
  readonly tags: SqlTagRepository
  readonly productTags: SqlProductTagRepository
  readonly auditLog: SqlAuditLogRepository
  /** Runs `work` with the repositories of the transaction; commits when it ends, rolls back when it throws. */
  transaction<T>(work: (uow: UnitOfWork) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
}

/** The repositories over one database: the application's, or one of its transactions. */
export class SqlUnitOfWork implements UnitOfWork {
  readonly customers: SqlCustomerRepository
  readonly categories: SqlCategoryRepository
  readonly products: SqlProductRepository
  readonly orders: SqlOrderRepository
  readonly orderLines: SqlOrderLineRepository
  readonly tags: SqlTagRepository
  readonly productTags: SqlProductTagRepository
  readonly auditLog: SqlAuditLogRepository

  constructor(readonly db: Executor) {
    this.customers = new SqlCustomerRepository(db)
    this.categories = new SqlCategoryRepository(db)
    this.products = new SqlProductRepository(db)
    this.orders = new SqlOrderRepository(db)
    this.orderLines = new SqlOrderLineRepository(db)
    this.tags = new SqlTagRepository(db)
    this.productTags = new SqlProductTagRepository(db)
    this.auditLog = new SqlAuditLogRepository(db)
  }

  /** Every write is committed at once: this only groups the code. */
  transaction<T>(work: (uow: UnitOfWork) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    return work(this)
  }
}
